tb21_profile.skill: Configure two real daemons (Postfix MTA and Mailman3) and the transport between them so that address-driven list operations -- join, leave, post, with confirmation replies -- actually flow to local unix mailboxes
tb21_profile.domain: Linux mail stack: Postfix main.cf/master.cf and aliases, Mailman3 mailman.cfg and runners, LMTP/local delivery, /var/mail mbox, service supervision
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service end to end: multi-daemon integration verified by driving the real protocol and reading the resulting mailboxes

verifier_notes: No grade I disagreed with. Worth noting for the merge: CalibForge's mail-server family is unusually well verified for a configure-a-service genre -- eight of the nine I ranked are strong with 4-9 pinned assertions, which for this kind of task means the tests actually send and read mail rather than grepping a config file. The one exception, system-administration_20260607_104421_006, is weak (3 pinned of 16) and I ranked it ninth partly for that. TMax's mailing-list family is mostly mock SMTP sinks rather than real MTAs, and several of its closest-by-wording entries (task_000472_bda99d41, task_006143_6d8cc883, task_003053_1f939255, task_006682_2131f432) are FREE; all are excluded.

notes: CalibForge decisively beats the old pool here and takes 8 of the final 10. It contains an entire Postfix+Dovecot mail-server family -- at least a dozen tasks, most graded strong -- covering fresh setup, virtual domains, and repairing a half-configured stack. Nothing in the v1 pool comes close: TMax's 'mailing list server' tasks are almost all mock SMTP sinks on unprivileged ports, and TerminalWorld/RTS offer only generic install-and-configure-a-daemon transfer. Terminal-Lego contributes one real win, task_10797 on newaliases/postalias, which is the Postfix alias mechanism TB2.1 depends on; the rest of its mail content is client-side SMTP/TLS in C# and PHP and should be discounted. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have nothing on mail-server configuration; I ranked them on config-file-loading and daemon-lifecycle bugs and nothing there exceeds overall 2, so the merge step should not draw from them for this task. Recursive-Task-Synthesis's best offering is the Samba AD desired-state family (membership management against a live directory daemon) plus one asterisk/kamailio two-places-must-agree config task; all absent-graded.
